summary: Token-driven banner refactor is clean, correct, and consistent with the WP-004 badge-tokenisation pattern. All four banner types (error, success, info, stale) are fully tokenised with --color-banner-{type}-{role} tokens defined in :root (light) and [data-theme="dark"] (dark). Run-event severity rules confirm token-driven via semantic --color-ready/in-progress/blocked/complete; grep confirms zero residual [data-theme="dark"] override blocks for all target selectors. Comment-card priority rules were already token-driven via --color-priority-* — correctly identified as already-complete. No blocking issues. No Fix-Forward changes applied.

comments.note: The light-mode .reset-modal-banner uses color: #92400e (amber-800) while --color-banner-stale-fg is #78350f (amber-900). These are similar but not identical, confirming the Developer's recommendation to create a dedicated --color-banner-warn-* token set rather than reusing --color-banner-stale-* tokens. Direct substitution would introduce a subtle visual change — a future WP should make an explicit colour decision before tokenising this component.

Minor token set asymmetry worth documenting: error and success banners intentionally reuse semantic --color-blocked and --color-complete for their foreground colour (no dedicated -fg token), while info and stale define dedicated --color-banner-{type}-fg tokens. This is correct design since blocked/complete already adapt in dark mode, but a short inline comment in the token block header would help future maintainers understand the divergence.
No issues — code is clean and consistent.
